Affective Envelope Follower

I built this Glitch Voice prototype to explore how changes in vocal expression could control live effects alongside loudness. A pretrained audEERING wav2vec 2.0 model estimates arousal, valence, and dominance from the microphone. I use those estimates as continuous controls for processing the same voice in Max/MSP.

View project source on GitHub ↗

Signal flow

  1. MicrophoneCapture mono audio at 16 kHz.
  2. Python + wav2vec 2.0Estimate arousal, valence, and dominance on rolling 1-second windows with a 250 ms hop.
  3. OSCSend the latest smoothed values from a dedicated thread at a configurable rate, 30 Hz by default.
  4. Max/MSPMap the estimates to effect parameters and triggers in the live vocal patch.

Live affect monitor

Mapping voice to effects

I mapped arousal to distortion, valence to reverb and delay, and dominance to granulation. I also used arousal thresholds to switch between different breath layers. These mappings let the performer hear how changes in the model’s estimates alter the processed voice.

Smoothing and response time

I gated descriptor updates by RMS level and smoothed the estimates to reduce jitter. In the conference talk, I reported an initial response after about 0.4–0.6 seconds and a stable value after about 1.5–2.5 seconds. Smoothing made the controls steadier, with a slower response to sudden vocal changes.

I demonstrated this prototype at Co-Creativity in Music, Sound, and AI at UC Riverside in June 2026.
